title: Pointed lifting torsors modulo global translation
statement: Let C be a site with terminal object T and an object U, with pointed torsors as in [def-amb-torsor-with-section]. Assume abelian-group sheafification exists and its local equivalences are exactly the locally bijective morphisms. Let 0→G→E→Q→0 be short exact. A framed lift is a pair (s,b), where s∈Q(T) and b∈E(U) maps to s restricted to U. It determines the G-torsor of lifts of s with specified section b. Two framed lifts (s,b),(s′,b′) determine isomorphic pointed torsors if and only if there is x∈E(T) with d(x)=s′−s and x|U=b′−b. If E is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], every pointed G-torsor has such a presentation; consequently their isomorphism classes are the quotient of framed lifts by this translation relation. The zero frame represents the trivial torsor with its zero section. More generally, two maps from a G-torsor to an abelian sheaf with the same G-equivariance have invariant difference, which descends to a global section and computes the difference of their prescribed quotient images.

proof.text: Use the absolute lifting-torsor presentation exists_equiv_lifts in the torsor classification [lem-sc-torsor-h1], applied to the given short exact sequence with E injective. Transport the specified section along the resulting torsor isomorphism. This proves surjectivity of framed presentations.

proof.text: For an equivariant isomorphism F of lifting torsors, the section F(t)−t is unchanged by replacing t with g+t. The existing invariant-section descent for a torsor therefore glues these differences to x∈E(T). Apply d and evaluate at b to get d(x)=s′−s and x|U=b′−b. Conversely translation by x is a natural equivariant isomorphism, with inverse translation by −x, and the second equality preserves the chosen section. The same invariant-difference calculation works for any two equally equivariant maps into an abelian sheaf.

proof.text: Take the quotient by pointed isomorphism and use the proved surjectivity to obtain the equivalence of classes. For the zero frame, the kernel identification G≅ker(d) identifies its lifting torsor with G and carries zero to zero.

theorem FramedLift.isIsomorphic_iff (z z' : FramedLift hT hS U) :
    WithSection.IsIsomorphic z.toPair z'.toPair ↔
      ∃ x : E.obj.obj (op T),
        d.hom.app (op T) x = z'.1 - z.1 ∧
        E.obj.map (hT.from U).op x = z'.2.1 - z.2.1
